candidate_relations.reason: The immunohistochemical profile (SOX10+, S100+, GCDFP-15+, PASD+, AR moderate positive, E-Cadherin+) with vesicular/tubular/striated arrangement patterns on FNAC is characteristic of acinic cell carcinoma, a rare special-type breast carcinoma with serous acinar differentiation. Invasive ductal carcinoma NOS is a distinct and incompatible histological subtype that lacks these defining salivary gland-type markers and morphological features. While both are invasive breast malignancies, the specific subtype designation conflicts.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Invasive ductal carcinoma NOS is a different histological subtype from acinic cell carcinoma of the breast

case_quality_flags: Rare special-type breast carcinoma with salivary gland-like differentiation; IHC panel strongly supports acinic cell carcinoma over IDC-NOS
FNAC morphology (vesicular, tubular, striated patterns) and marker profile (SOX10, S100, GCDFP-15, PASD) are diagnostically distinctive
